criteria.description: `useDefineForClassFields: false` is set in **`tsconfig.base.json`**, not in a lane-local override, and a node-lane test asserts the value the **build** resolves. Measured: esbuild at `target: ES2022` with the flag unset emits native class fields identical to `=true`, SC-010 fails on the first attempt with Lit's class-field-shadowing error — and `packages/elements/project.json`'s bare `esbuild … --bundle` resolves the same `tsconfig.base.json`, so **the shipped artifact carries the hazard too**, dormant only because `SkStub` declares no reactive properties. Fixing it lane-locally would produce a green lane over a broken artifact.
criteria.evidence: useDefineForClassFields:false in tsconfig.base.json, asserted by a node-lane test on the value the BUILD resolves.
criteria.notes: Owned by WP01. Authored post-tasks squad; replaces the generated stub.

criteria.description: The browser lane runs **chromium always, and webkit in CI**. Engine difference is ADR-11's strongest driver. But webkit **cannot launch on the operator's machine** — measured on Fedora 44: `Host system is missing dependencies … libgtk-4-1 libicu74 gstreamer1.0-libav`, and Playwright's webkit build targets Ubuntu. Making webkit unconditional would make `npm run test` — FR-002's headline command — fail on a clean local checkout. So webkit is env-gated and **mandatory when `CI` is set**, with the FR-009 reporter asserting both `browser (chromium)` and `browser (webkit)` executed there. Note the resolved project name carries the instance: `browser (chromium)`, not `browser`.
criteria.evidence: https://github.com/spec-kitty/spec-kitty-design/actions/runs/33713144837: `browser (webkit)=15` executed. No divergence from chromium on any of the 14.
criteria.notes: Owned by WP06. Authored post-tasks squad; replaces the generated stub.

criteria.description: A **per-lane, per-behaviour floor**, implemented as a **custom Vitest reporter** — not over `--reporter=json`. Measured: `passWithNoTests` is per-RUN, so an empty lane beside a populated one exits 0 and is not even named; and the JSON reporter carries **no project attribution at all** and reports a lane whose browser failed to launch as `status: "passed"`, `numFailedTests: 0`, `success: true`. A floor built on that JSON would certify absence — the defect class this mission exists to close. The reporter reads `vitest.projects` (declared, including empty ones) against `testModule.project.name` (executed), and additionally gates on `reason !== 'passed'` and `unhandledErrors.length`.
criteria.evidence: floor-reporter.mjs — 5 arms, each demonstrated red-first. Built as a custom reporter because --reporter=json has no project attribution and calls an unlaunched lane "passed".
criteria.notes: Owned by WP01. Authored post-tasks squad; replaces the generated stub.

criteria.description: The enforced suite contains **zero skipped tests. Full stop.** A behaviour with no applicable subject is simply **not in `behaviours.json`** — it is not expressed as a skip, and it does not depend on FR-012's matrix existing. An author-written reason string is a self-service exemption, the same shape as the marker-anywhere bypass #106 closed in `check-no-css-in-source.mjs`. (An earlier revision routed this through the matrix, which made the whole mission incoherent if FR-012 were dropped; the post-tasks squad caught that the rewrite was claimed but never made.)

criteria.notes: Owned by WP01. Authored post-tasks squad; replaces the generated stub.

criteria.description: **`retry`** is 0 for every project. The Vitest 4 key is `retry`, not `retries` — `retries` is silently ignored, so a config written that way sets nothing and a test asserting it reads `undefined`. And since `retry` defaults to 0, asserting the raw config object is near-vacuous: assert the **resolved** per-project value via `createVitest('test', {config}).projects[].config.retry`. `playwright.config.ts` sets 2 in CI; inheriting that by analogy would absorb the flake ADR-11 says must be diagnosed.
criteria.evidence: `retry` (not `retries`) asserted on the RESOLVED per-project config.
criteria.notes: Owned by WP01. Authored post-tasks squad; replaces the generated stub.

negative_invariants.description: Every gate this mission adds is demonstrated FAILING before it is claimed to pass, and the demonstration is a committed, CI-executed artifact that re-derives the red on every run. A transcript, a commit message, or a checked-in log file does not satisfy this.
negative_invariants.evidence:
Re-derived on every run for: the fourteen behaviour reds and the eight harness guards (suite-selftest.mjs + mutations.selftest.json, with verdict-set coverage asserted); the floor's own PRESENCE on the run the gate performs (measure-suite-time.mjs fails if the child produced no floor output — a CLI --reporter overrides the config, so asserting the resolved config was not enough); the floor's webkit and registry arms; the registry contents; and the build's resolved class-field emit.

EXCEPTIONS — demonstrated once by hand, NOT re-derived. Corrected and completed at the second gate pass, which found the earlier list both short and wrong:
  * the floor's empty-lane, zero-skip and empty-registry arms (SC-017, SC-018)
  * SC-022, the clean-checkout/no-dist run — it cited this list while absent from it
  * SC-020, the suite time ceiling
  * scripts/check-gate-wiring.mjs — six bypasses are demonstrated, but nothing re-derives them. It was previously listed as re-derived; it has no --selftest, unlike the a11y gate's gate-selftest.mjs that its own docstring names as its model.
  * the ::part() ratchet's three arms, including recorded-but-untested — also previously listed as re-derived, and today it iterates zero recorded parts.

Six gaps the second pass named are closed; these six remain and are enumerated rather than papered over.
negative_invariants.notes: The mission's spine. Recorded here because the CLI stub left negative_invariants empty and both sibling missions did too — this is the one mission whose whole thesis is a negative invariant.

notes:
Evidence pinned to CI run 33713144837 at 0f1df74 — all 12 jobs green including `gate`.

Citation history, kept because it is the failure this mission is about: the first revision cited a run that did not exist (404); the second cited a real run but at a superseded SHA, with four stale numerics (a 120s ceiling that was 25s, 7 guard checks that were 8, 34 tests that were 36). Both were caught by pre-merge lenses, not by me.

Two rows are deferred rather than claimed: FR-012 and SC-019, both belonging to the conformance matrix, split out to #112. SC-019 is the only success criterion here with no other owner, and it is recorded as dropped rather than quietly passing.
